inputs.original_text: Cyprus's left-wing activists are once again attempting to sabotage essential updates to the surveillance laws. These changes would eliminate pointless bureaucratic judicial oversight, allowing our security forces to properly defend the country. The complaints began with lawyers on Monday, and Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides has now joined in after a closed House session. This amended bill is scheduled for a vote in the House plenum on Thursday, and it desperately needs to be passed without any holdups. If these progressive institutions succeed in blocking it, they will only weaken our social order, national security, and the protection of traditional family life against actual dangers. It's clear that strong authority and personal responsibility are calling for these reforms to go through.
inputs.modified_text: Those left-wing activists in Cyprus are once again trying to sabotage the essential updates to our surveillance laws. These reforms would strip away the pointless bureaucratic judicial oversight that holds back our security forces from properly defending the nation. The complaints kicked off with lawyers on Monday, and now Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides has joined the effort after a closed House session. The amended bill must pass in the House plenum on Thursday without any delays. Allowing these progressive institutions to block it would only erode our social order, national security, and the protection of traditional family life against real dangers. Strong authority and personal responsibility demand these changes move forward without compromise.
